# Gloss that echoes the form

This check finds senses whose gloss is only the entry's form written in capitals: `XYZ` on `xyz-`, or the capitals followed by a dotted suffix (`XYZ.V`). Hyphens and `=` are ignored, and any allomorph form of the entry counts. A gloss that adds only a dotted suffix is the mark of a clone entry made to carry a feature. A gloss written in the same case as the form, such as a proper name or a loanword (`radar` on `radar`), is not reported, because it can be a real gloss.

## Analyse

Read the entry in `allomorph-context` and compare its forms with the sense's glosses in every analysis writing system. Process affixes with no form text are not read, because there is no form to echo.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask what the morpheme means or does, so the gloss can say it. Include the entry, its form and the gloss that echoes it. A dotted suffix suggests a clone entry: ask whether it should be merged with its homograph.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding. Replace the gloss with a meaningful one in FieldWorks, or merge the clone into its homograph.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the sense is no longer listed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Advises making a gloss as meaningful as possible; it does not rule on any particular gloss, so the finding asks rather than concludes.
